title: Can I mail a gift box without putting it in another box?
summary: Use a separate shipping carton for a decorative gift box unless the box was designed to travel on its own. A lift-off lid can separate, and the paper wrap can pick up scuffs or shipping labels.
buyerNote: Pack the finished gift in a sturdy outer carton with cushioning on every side. Close the carton and gently tilt it. If the gift box slides into a wall, adjust the cushioning before sealing.

title: What size gift bag will fit my box?
summary: Compare the box footprint with the inside base of the opened bag. The side gusset opens to give the bag depth. A tall, wide bag can still be too shallow for the box to sit flat.
buyerNote: For a box with a 22 × 12 cm base, a bag that opens only 10 cm deep is too small in that orientation. Try the loaded box in the bag. It should settle flat, clear the handle knots and come out without tearing the corners.

title: How do I keep a necklace from tangling in a gift box?
summary: Fasten the clasp and keep the chain in two separate channels on a necklace card or insert. Seat the pendant at the front and gather the spare chain behind the card so it cannot cross the pendant.
buyerNote: Use one card per necklace. Close the box and tilt it gently, then reopen it. If a fine chain has slipped free, try closer-fitting slots or a small soft pouch behind the insert to contain the spare length.

title: What kind of gift box fits a single bottle of cognac?
summary: Choose a single-bottle presentation box with a fitted insert that supports the base and body of your particular bottle. Two 700 ml bottles can have very different shoulders, widths and stopper heights.
buyerNote: Measure the filled bottle with its stopper in place. Check that a broad decanter cannot rotate in the insert and that a tall stopper clears the lid. For delivery, arrange a suitable bottle shipper separately.

title: How should I store folding gift boxes until I need them?
summary: Keep unassembled folding gift boxes flat, dry and supported across the full base. Leave the backing on adhesive corner tabs until you are ready to assemble each box.
buyerNote: Slide the blanks into a shallow carton on a shelf. Placing a small, heavy object on the middle of the stack can dent several lids at once. Keep any permanently glued boxes assembled.

title: How can I tell corrugated cardboard from paperboard?
summary: Look at a cut edge. Corrugated board has a wavy paper layer between flat liners. Ordinary solid paperboard shows a compact edge without open channels.
buyerNote: Compare the edge of a shipping carton with the flap on a cereal box. Very fine corrugations can be hard to see from the printed face, so inspect the flap edge under a light.

title: Can I pack two ceramic mugs in the same box?
summary: Yes, if each mug has its own cushioning and the two cannot touch. Give each handle its own clear space. A handle pressed against the other mug or a hard divider is a likely chip point.
buyerNote: Place the wrapped mugs in separate compartments before closing the box. Press lightly on one compartment and check that the other mug stays still. For parcel delivery, use a sturdy shipping carton with cushioning around the pair.

title: Can I reuse the box my order came in for a return?
summary: Usually, yes, if the retailer accepts it and the shipping box is still sturdy, dry and able to close properly. Follow the retailer’s instructions if it supplies a particular mailer or packaging for the return.
buyerNote: Check the corners, folds and bottom seam. Remove or fully cover old address labels and barcodes, put just the current return label on a flat face, and reseal the seams with packing tape.

title: Can I recycle shiny wrapping paper?
summary: Plain paper gift wrap is often accepted with paper recycling. Shiny film or laminated wrapping can need a different disposal route. Your local recycling programme determines what goes in your bin.
buyerNote: Remove ribbons, bows and tags before sorting the wrap. If a sheet has a plastic layer and your local programme does not accept it, save it to wrap a smaller gift.

title: Can I put homemade chocolates straight into a gift box?
summary: Place chocolates in cups, a tray or a liner sold for direct food contact. An ordinary decorative box can hold that inner pack, but its paper, inks and glue may have been chosen only for appearance.
buyerNote: For a box of nine truffles, try a three-by-three tray sized to the actual chocolates. Close the lid over the tallest topping and reopen it to check that the finish stays intact.

title: Is tissue paper enough to protect a fragile gift in the mail?
summary: Tissue paper makes a neat wrap and can separate delicate surfaces. Thin sheets alone give a glass or ceramic gift too little protection from impacts during parcel handling.
buyerNote: Wrap the item for presentation first. Then immobilise it in a fitted insert or suitable cushioning inside a sturdy shipping box. Check that no glass edge or ceramic handle can reach a wall.

title: How can I close a gift box without sticking tape to it?
summary: Wrap a paper band or ribbon around the closed gift box. Tape the band to itself on the underside, or tie the ribbon in a bow so the recipient can open the box without peeling its finish.
buyerNote: Use a strip of scrap paper to measure the path around the lid and base. Allow an overlap for a paper band. For a ribbon, tie a trial bow before cutting the final length.

title: How do I stop items moving around in a hamper box?
summary: Use a snug divider or fitted tray for the heaviest items, then fill the small spaces around lighter ones. A handful of decorative shredded paper can settle under a jar and allow it to roll.
buyerNote: Try the arrangement with the actual contents. Put glass jars in separate compartments and keep them away from crushable packets. Gently tilt the closed hamper in each direction and listen for contact.

title: How can I tell which way a drawer gift box opens?
summary: Look for the exposed short edge of the inner tray. A ribbon tab, thumb notch or visible join between the tray and sleeve usually marks where to pull.
buyerNote: Support the sleeve with one hand and draw the tray straight out with the other. Stop if it binds and check for a paper band around the sleeve before pulling harder.

title: Should I choose a paper insert or a foam insert for a gift?
summary: A folded paperboard insert can hold a light item with a regular shape. A shaped foam cavity can support heavier or irregular pieces that need more restraint. The right choice depends on where the insert touches the product.
buyerNote: Try the insert with the actual gift. Check the widest edges, any glass corners and the space for your fingers. You should be able to remove the gift without pulling on a cap, spout or other fragile part.

title: How should I package a candle in a glass jar as a gift?
summary: Choose a box with a level base and an insert that supports the jar and keeps it from sliding. Include the lid when you measure the candle so it cannot press into the closed gift box.
buyerNote: If the set includes a metal snuffer or a second candle, give each item its own compartment. For posting, put the presentation box in a cushioned outer carton and check that the jar cannot knock against anything hard.

title: What is the best way to pack shoes in a gift box?
summary: Set the shoes heel to toe when their shape allows it and slip tissue between surfaces that could rub. Buckles, metal trim and heels need enough room to clear the other shoe and the lid.
buyerNote: Try the tallest shoe in the pair with its stuffing and dust bag in place. Close the box without pressing down. If the upper creases or a buckle marks the tissue, change the arrangement or use a deeper box.

title: What does post-consumer recycled cardboard mean?
summary: Post-consumer recycled board contains fibre recovered after a product has been used, such as material from collected boxes. A recycled-content claim describes the source of the fibre.
buyerNote: Look for the percentage and the component it refers to. A box with a recycled greyboard core can still have a different paper wrap, a ribbon or a foam insert. Sort those parts according to your local recycling guidance.
